extracted.intended_audience: adult writers (beginner to advanced) seeking creative-writing classes, workshops, publication guidance, and youth writing camps
extracted.subtask_description: A catalog of multi-genre creative-writing classes, workshops, intensives, and youth camps describing learning objectives, craft principles, publication/submission guidance, and expected participant outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire & need as character foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Figuring out desire and need can serve as the foundation for strong character backstory and motivation, as well as plot points that connect the beginning, middle and end of your novel or memoir.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-session workshop with exercises relating to desire and need to strengthen backstory and create organic forward motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attunement to the more-than-human world
rubrics_metrics.description: Use writing prompts derived from forest bathing, bird noticing, and other practices meant to attune us to the more-than-human world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants will leave with three to four drafts of poems or short prose and skills for writing about nature and your place within it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry and performance for social change
rubrics_metrics.description: Use poetry and performance to open eyes, preserve stories, change hearts, and create new narratives that enact social change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore thematic 'R words' (Resilience, Resistance, Revelation, Rise Up, Revolution, Reparations, Restoration) and write together toward change-oriented work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics of writing about loved ones
rubrics_metrics.description: How do we tell our truths and stay compassionate to theirs? How do we write with humor, courage, rage, or beauty about the ones we love(d)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study renowned writers for inspiration; learn to find moments and voices best suited to your story and navigate ethical perils of uncomfortable truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafting personal experience into a stage-worthy story
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to craft personal experience into a compelling and captivating story and examine how the written and spoken word differ when adding performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-part workshop: craft on the page, then read aloud and add performance elements to engage audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key elements of short humor pieces (McSweeney’s-style)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the key elements of writing brief, McSweeney’s-style humor pieces and explore publication options in the humor-writing market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to discuss comedic influences, provide favorite examples, collaborate with peers; no experience necessary but other-genre experience is a plus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of themed prompts & flash forms for nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Use prompts linked to weekly themes (road trips, mix tapes, romances, pilgrimages, quests) mashed with short/flash forms (hermit crabs, visual essays, abecedarians, collage, erasure/found pieces) to generate a portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focused on nonfiction but all genres welcome; students will leave with a portfolio of new starts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming writing anxiety and producing output
rubrics_metrics.description: Address blank-page anxiety with techniques and practices to begin or finish projects, producing substantial pages and receiving feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students will leave class with 25 pages written toward a project and extensive instructor feedback; study writers who admit to anxiety and practice techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to revise and how to finish a book
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to distinguish when to revise and when not to, identify productive vs counterproductive questions, and find ways to re-invigorate yourself to complete a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asynchronous course with pacing through online sessions; practical strategies to sustain long-form projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using literary experiments to break creative blocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply experiments (flip the trope, shift perspective, trespass boundaries) to break entrenched patterns and free creative thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring stalled drafts and let them run off-leash; focused on nonfiction but open to all genres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative grammar: learn conventions and deliberate rule-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Most good writing conforms to standard English conventions, but great writers break rules with precision and intent; learn the rules and practice effective divergence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review conventions (e.g., punctuating dialogue), study examples of effective 'broken' rules, write/revise short passages and practice rule-breaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using memory, ghosts, and the residue of past experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Get familiar with familiars and the stories that haunt peripheries of awareness; generate work that lets ghosts speak, from fantastical to lyrical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use works by Toni Morrison, Neil Gaiman, García Márquez as guideposts to produce new work that pulls aside the veil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerability as a creative practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore vulnerability defined as uncertainty, risk, and emotional exposure to move through artistic fear and get writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exercises to visualize projects and approaches; bring one in-progress piece and leave with a clear path forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid forms: lyric essay and braided personal narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Radicalize personal narrative by intertwining poetry and memoir to produce lyric essays and hybrid braided forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in experimental writing exercises and share stories; celebrate personal story and lyricism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflecting collectively on recent shared experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Use writing prompts and group discussion to reflect on life before and during the pandemic, articulate impacts/changes, and imagine next stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process workshop toggling between inner and collective experiences; prompted writing and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notebooks as generative practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate how notebooks can feed creative work and even serve as creative work themselves; study written/illustrated correspondence and journal-keeping essays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine generative exercises, workshops, and examples; expect to investigate outside comfort zone and gain creative-practice insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using mythology and textual avatars to inspire writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn to mythological texts and episodes (e.g., Vishnu’s avatars) to fuel multi-genre creative pieces without prior subject knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part-generative, part-analytical: read key texts/episodes and use them to generate diverse work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminar-style close-reading to illuminate craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage in book-club-like seminars led by instructors to discuss books as art, resistance, cultural commentary, and historical artifact with craft-focused conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss points of craft in each week’s reading and compile optional field-note prompts; registered students receive book discount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blending ideas with plot (narrative layering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Study how an author (e.g., Sigrid Nunez) blends ideas with plot, using chapter outlines to analyze construction of character, conflict, and theme and apply techniques to works-in-progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a detailed chapter outline as a home base for discussion and application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing basics for BIPOC writers (agents & editors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of the publishing business geared toward BIPOC writers, including subverting the 'white gaze', building support networks, writing query letters, finding an agent who champions your voice, and advocating for your project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes agents/editors as guests, opportunities to pitch selected projects, and practical insider perspectives from industry professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitching essays and articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop strong pitches, angles, and relationships with editors to increase acceptance rates; learn negotiating contracts and the craft of pitching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step-by-step guide; leave with a strong pitch ready to send and a list of editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-to-end publishing process awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Walk through the publication process from getting an agent to hitting shelves: querying, copy editing, conference attendance, evaluating agents, and interpreting editor feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A-Z course offering practical answers to common publishing questions and decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir book proposal components
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn each component of a memoir book proposal and strategies to craft a proposal that gains the attention of agents and editors, plus tips for a compelling query letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-session focused on practical proposal writing strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions strategy & application materials (for BIPOC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find and submit to literary journals, fellowships, residencies, and grants; develop a strong artist statement, bio, and project proposal; uncover resources to target opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes an interactive submission party to practice sending applications and build a submission plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculative fiction publishing intensive
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive overview of publishing for speculative fiction writers, covering opportunities across lengths and requiring a short synopsis for small-group pitch exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daylong seminar with special guests and a pitch exercise; applicable to a broad speculative-fiction practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using imagination and signaling in memoir when memory fails
rubrics_metrics.description: When memory is not enough, use research, interviewing, fact-checking, and imagination, and explicitly cue readers when imagination is being used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative seminar studying writers who blend imagination and memory, with in-class writing sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding and developing a distinct writer’s voice
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's voice locates where humor and seriousness sit, what you believe in, why you write, and who/what you write about; study strong voices and try techniques to locate your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-hour generative seminar with examples (Joy Harjo, Lidia Yuknavitch, etc.), in-class prompts, optional sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir craft elements and practical production
rubrics_metrics.description: Memoir intensive topics: voice and vision, inviting readers in, narrative arc, thematic drive, collage techniques, scene-building, the publication process, and time-management for writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-day intensive including lecture, discussion, prompts, brainstorming, and participant workshops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral storytelling craft and performance-ready sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use personal material (humanity, embarrassing moments) to craft a six- to ten-minute showcase-able oral storytelling set through exercises and polishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-day course focused on deriving material and refining for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-animal studies in poetry for empathy and agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate to and write about animals to learn about empathy, language, and agency; read sample poems and generate work based on prompts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction to field; examples include Mary Oliver and others; options to share in group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploring desire and power structures in literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss themes of lust, vulnerability, shame, and their interaction with cultural power structures (whiteness, heteronormativity, cisgendering), and be encouraged to explore new forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should expect to leave with one to three workshopped pieces and greater confidence of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing poetry reviews and close-reading skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how a poetry review differs from other reviews, discover what kind of reviewer you are, and practice writing short reader reviews with support for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring books of poetry; exercises to develop review-writing craft and submission strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community classes & drop-in structured writing time
rubrics_metrics.description: Lower-cost/free community classes and drop-in write-ins offer less instruction but consistent, structured time and prompts to facilitate craft and community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for trying new genres, meeting teachers, or accessing writing time when regular classes are prohibitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission logistics and psychological supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Address barriers to submitting work: learn submission portals, use a rejection tracker, set submission goals, and review examples of cover letters and do's/don'ts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Walk away with clear submission goals and foundational tools to start submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting published work (PR for writers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seven-step framework for promoting published work: choosing digital platforms, simplifying content creation, and identifying personal strengths to maximize marketing online and at events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss platforms, content strategies, and strengths to leverage for publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative voice (La voz narrativa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative voice determines whether a story succeeds or fails — not just point of view but the manner of telling and what is left unsaid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read accomplished and unsuccessful voices, do creative exercises to find and refine voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sliding-scale & scholarship access for youth programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Scribes Summer Camp tuition offered on a sliding scale with full/partial scholarships available to make programs accessible; no application required for sliding scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Families pick price that works for their budget; more info at hugohouse.org/youth-programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Youth camps: craft and multimedia production skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Age-appropriate objectives: creative writing camps develop craft via curated texts and exercises; radio drama camps teach scriptwriting, vocal performance, foley, and audio editing; video-poem camps write poems and create short accompanying videos; comics camps teach visual storytelling fundamentals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most camps culminate in a presentation or final piece; some require outside filming or basic video skills; formats vary by age group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics & health policy for in-person classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Hugo House’s up-to-date in-person COVID-19 health and safety policies at registration; policies subject to change and classes may be moved online with notice to registrants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students will be notified via email of changes prior to class day; check hugohouse.org for current policies.
